issues.title: Bloom filter for sparse perfect-hash joins
issues.hypothesis: The main chain of q21 accounts for most of its time. Run alone without the subqueries, it takes 0.658s wall of the 0.835s query. In that chain, the lineitem l1 scan has no selective filter: FILTER (l_receiptdate>l_commitdate) emits 37.9M rows and the INNER join l_suppkey=s_suppkey (0.38s CPU) cuts them to 1.52M. The build side is supplier⋈nation with 4,009 keys spread over a key range of about 100K. That fits a perfect hash table (range <= 1M, physical_hash_join.cpp Finalize -> CanDoPerfectHashJoin). JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:769) returns false for any perfect hash table, on the reasoning that 'we expect good min/max pruning'. With 4% density spread over the whole range, min/max prunes nothing, so the probe-side scan decodes all its columns for all 60M rows. A 4-column lineitem scan measured 2.2-3.4s CPU, while a 2-column scan measured about 1.0s. A bloom filter on l_suppkey in the scan would drop about 96% of rows before the other columns are fetched (the scan fetches non-filter columns only for selected rows) and before the FILTER and the join probe run.
issues.plan: 1) In CanUseBloomFilter (src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp ~761), replace the unconditional `if (is_perfect_hashtable) return false;` with a density check. Allow the bloom filter for a perfect hash table only if the build is sparse: ht->Count() * 4 < build_range + 1, where build_range is the perfect_join_statistics.build_range that CanDoPerfectHashJoin has computed. Pass the range (or a bool `perfect_ht_is_sparse`) from PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize to FinalizeFilters and on to CanUseBloomFilter. All other conditions stay: build_side_has_filter, probe estimate > build count, single EQUAL condition, no cast. 2) The bloom filter is filled during the regular finalize (JoinHashTable::Finalize initialises it when should_build_bloom_filter is set; InsertHashes fills it; HashJoinFinalizeEvent::FinishEvent pushes the deferred filters). The perfect path skips ScheduleFinalize (Finalize ~1017), so when use_perfect_hash is set and sink.deferred_bloom_filters is not empty, still call sink.ScheduleFinalize(pipeline, event). Keep perfect_join_executor so the probe still uses the perfect hash table. Building the pointer table for a small build (<=256K rows when sparse) is cheap. Check that BuildPerfectHashTable does not consume the data collection; it only scans it. If finalizing alongside the perfect hash table proves unsafe, fall back to this: when the build is sparse and a bloom filter is deferred, set use_perfect_hash=false (reset the executor and take the normal path). 3) Confirm with `dbe-tool sql "EXPLAIN ANALYZE <main chain of q21>"` that the lineitem scan shows `l_suppkey IN BF` and that the FILTER above it gets far fewer than 37.9M rows.
issues.expected_gain: q21: -15..-30%. The l1 lineitem scan should drop from about 2-3s CPU to under 1s, FILTER from 60M to about 2.4M rows, and the suppkey join probe from 37.9M to about 1.5M rows.
issues.generality: Helps any star or snowflake join where a filtered dimension with dense integer keys (a perfect-hash candidate) is joined to a large fact table: dimension filters like nation/region/category on TPC-H/SSB/TPC-DS. Today those joins never get a bloom filter. Could be slower: queries where the build keys are sparse but nearly every probe value matches, so the bloom filter filters nothing. SelectivityOptionalFilter (BF_THRESHOLD) turns itself off after its check window, so the cost is bounded to a short trial plus building the pointer table and bloom filter for the small build.
issues.risk: Medium-low. Main correctness risk is running the regular finalize alongside the perfect hash table (finalized flag, pinned data collection). The fallback (dropping the perfect hash table when sparse) is trivially correct. Bloom filters are optional filters, so the results do not depend on them.
